subject.title: fix(memory): recover real on-disk path for slugified QMD search results

question: Should an active QMD slug alias authorize reading a unique slug-equivalent filesystem path that is not itself the active indexed row, and where should that canonical mapping be established?
rationale: This changes both the indexed-read trust boundary and the lifecycle location of alias discovery; tests cannot determine whether inactive QMD records, a prepared mapping, or filesystem recovery is the intended permanent contract.

options.title: Prepare an index-backed alias map
options.body: Resolve unique aliases from authoritative QMD records during index or collection refresh and authorize only the resulting prepared mapping during search and read.

options.title: Approve bounded filesystem recovery
options.body: Keep filesystem recovery only after owner approval and add live native-QMD, symlink, collision, and large-tree latency proof demonstrating that the broader boundary is safe.

options.title: Wait for upstream canonical paths
options.body: Pause the TypeScript workaround and fix or upgrade native QMD so active records retain real filesystem paths.

recommendation.title: Prepare an index-backed alias map
recommendation.body: Resolve unique aliases from authoritative QMD records during index or collection refresh and authorize only the resulting prepared mapping during search and read.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent substantial QMD lifecycle and collection work makes this the strongest available owner signal for deciding where alias normalization belongs.
